checks.actualAlgorithm: Track used digits for every row, column and subgrid. Repeatedly choose an empty cell with the fewest legal candidates, try each candidate, and undo failed choices. Only initially empty cells are assigned, preserving clues.

Every attempted candidate is absent from all three relevant tables, so each placement preserves Sudoku validity and every original clue remains untouched. Failed branches undo both the cell and its table entries. Trying every legal candidate is complete: any valid completion must choose one of them. The fewest-candidates heuristic changes only search order, not which completions are possible.

Every clue is preserved and every unit is valid; the adapter returns true.

Each recursive choice fills an empty cell, giving at most n choices at each of e branching levels; the local candidate-check cost multiplies that tree size.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Map each binary counter value i to i XOR (i shifted right once). This reflected Gray-code mapping visits every bit pattern once and changes one bit between consecutive outputs.
checks.correctness: The map g(i)=i XOR (i>>1) is invertible on b-bit values, so all 2^b outputs are distinct. Consecutive binary values differ by a carry run; XORing each with its right shift cancels that run except at one bit, giving consecutive Gray values Hamming distance one. For b>0 the reflected sequence also closes cyclically: its last value is 1<<(b-1), one bit from zero. The bank adapter only requires consecutive output pairs.
checks.workedTrace: For 3 bits, i=0..7 maps to [0,1,3,2,6,7,5,4]. For example 3 XOR 2 = 1 and 2 XOR 6 = 4, each a single set bit. All eight values occur exactly once.
checks.edgeCases: Zero bits gives the single value [0]. Do not repeat a pattern or use values outside the b-bit range. The output has exponential size even though each value is computed in constant word operations.
checks.timeDerivation: O(2^b) time for b bits. Formula variants perform constant word operations per one of 2^b outputs; search variants have the separately stated branching bound.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(1) auxiliary space, plus O(2^b) output space. Formula variants retain only loop state beyond output; search retains its history and path stack.

checks.correctness: The map g(i)=i XOR (i>>1) is invertible on b-bit values, so all 2^b outputs are distinct. Consecutive binary values differ by a carry run; XORing each with its right shift cancels that run except at one bit, giving consecutive Gray values Hamming distance one. For b>0 the reflected sequence also closes cyclically: its last value is 1<<(b-1), one bit from zero. The bank adapter only requires consecutive output pairs.
checks.workedTrace: For 3 bits, i=0..7 maps to [0,1,3,2,6,7,5,4]. For example 3 XOR 2 = 1 and 2 XOR 6 = 4, each a single set bit. All eight values occur exactly once.
checks.edgeCases: Zero bits gives the single value [0]. Do not repeat a pattern or use values outside the b-bit range. The output has exponential size even though each value is computed in constant word operations.
checks.timeDerivation: O(2^b) time for b bits. Formula variants perform constant word operations per one of 2^b outputs; search variants have the separately stated branching bound.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(1) auxiliary space, plus O(2^b) output space. Formula variants retain only loop state beyond output; search retains its history and path stack.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Find the lower bound: the first position whose value is at least k. It is the first occurrence if it equals k; otherwise the target is absent.
checks.correctness: The half-open interval [left,right) retains the possible lower-bound position. Every discarded left value is less than k; every discarded right value is at least k. At convergence left is the first position with value at least k, so it is the first occurrence exactly when its value equals k.

checks.edgeCases: An empty array returns -1. Repeated targets return their first index. A lower bound at array length means the target is absent. Targets below the minimum still require an equality check.
checks.timeDerivation: O(log n). Each iteration halves the candidate interval, hence logarithmically many comparisons.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(1). Only two endpoints, a midpoint and possibly one saved index are retained.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Binary search the interval from zero to max(1,x). Compare middle with x/middle to avoid overflow from squaring; stop when floating-point rounding prevents further interval refinement.
checks.correctness: For x>0, the initial interval [0,max(1,x)] contains √x. For a positive midpoint, midpoint≤x/midpoint is equivalent to midpoint²≤x without overflowing a square. Replacing the appropriate endpoint preserves containment. Repeated bisection narrows the bracket until floating-point resolution prevents further progress.
checks.workedTrace: For x=6.25, start with [0,6.25]. Midpoint 3.125 exceeds 6.25/3.125=2, so the root lies below it. Repeated comparisons narrow the interval around 2.5, whose square is 6.25; return approximately 2.5.
checks.edgeCases: x=0 returns zero without dividing by a midpoint. Values between zero and one still use an upper bound of one. Division avoids overflow when x is very large. The judge compares floating-point answers with a relative tolerance.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Split the list with slow/fast pointers, sort both halves recursively, then merge their original nodes. Choosing the left node on equal values preserves the relative order of ties.
checks.correctness: Splitting decreases the list size, so induction gives two sorted halves. The merge repeatedly selects the least head, preserving sorted order and every original node. On equal values it selects from the left half first. Since all left-half nodes originally preceded right-half nodes, and recursive calls preserve their internal tie order, the complete merge sort is stable.
checks.workedTrace: Label the two 7-valued nodes in [7, 3, 7, 1] as 7a and 7b. The halves sort to [3, 7a] and [1, 7b]. Merging emits 1, then 3; at the tie it takes 7a before 7b. Return values [1, 3, 7, 7], with the original equal-valued nodes still in their original order.
checks.edgeCases: Null and one-node lists are already sorted. Repeated values must preserve node order, not merely sorted values. The list is split before recursion and original nodes are relinked rather than copied.
checks.timeDerivation: O(n log n) time. Each recursion level splits/merges O(n) nodes and balanced halves give O(log n) levels.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(log n) recursion space; nodes are reused. Recursion depth is logarithmic; merging relinks existing nodes and uses only a constant-size sentinel per active merge.
checks.callableAgreement: Callable: ListNode<int>? StableSortList(ListNode<int>? L). Returns the new head of the relinked original nodes; equal nodes retain identity order. The displayed JSON output serializes node values.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Sort the salaries. Treat the smaller salaries as fully paid, and divide the remaining target equally among the remaining employees. The first candidate cap no greater than the next salary is the answer. A target above the original payroll is impossible.
checks.correctness: After fixing the i smallest salaries, paid is their unchanged total. Any cap at least those salaries contributes paid plus cap times the remaining employee count. The first candidate at most the next salary satisfies this equation in the correct piecewise-linear segment; no smaller cap reaches the target.
checks.workedTrace: For salaries [5,10,20] and target 29, a cap below 5 cannot suffice. Pay 5 unchanged, then 10 unchanged; the remaining employee must receive 29−15=14. Cap 14 gives 5+10+14=29.
checks.edgeCases: A target above the original payroll returns −1. A target equal to the original total returns the largest salary. A zero target gives cap zero for a nonempty nonnegative salary list.
checks.timeDerivation: O(n log n) time. Sorting dominates a single pass through salaries and a constant-time cap calculation per position.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(n) auxiliary space for the sorted copy. Only a prefix total and candidate cap are needed beyond sorted storage.
checks.callableAgreement: Callable: double FindSalaryCap(int target_payroll, List<int> current_salaries). Sort a copy; caller input stays unchanged.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Store each value together with the maximum of its stack prefix. Pop reveals the previous prefix maximum immediately. Initialize clears the logical stack; the underlying value-tuple stack retains its allocated capacity.
checks.correctness: Every stored pair holds its pushed value and the maximum of the prefix ending at that entry. Push computes that prefix maximum from the old top and the new value. Pop removes exactly the last prefix, exposing the correct maximum for the remaining stack. Initialize clears every pair, and Empty checks whether any prefix remains. checks.actualAlgorithm: Encoding groups each maximal run and writes its decimal length followed by its character. Decoding accumulates all digits of the next length, then repeats the following nondigit character and resets the count.
checks.correctness: Encoding partitions the input into maximal equal-character runs, so each written count/character pair describes exactly one run. During decoding, count contains all decimal digits since the previous character; emitting that many copies reconstructs the corresponding run and resets the invariant. Nondigit input characters make the representation unambiguous.
checks.workedTrace: For decoded text "qqqqqqqqqqqqrr", Encoding counts twelve q characters and two r characters, returning "12q2r". Decoding accumulates digits 1 then 2 into count 12, emits twelve q characters, then emits two r characters. Both directions recover the other value.
checks.edgeCases: Empty text encodes and decodes to empty text. Run lengths may contain several decimal digits. A singleton run still writes count 1. Original text characters must be nondigits.
checks.timeDerivation: O(n + m) for input length n and produced output length m. Encoding visits each input character once; decoding scans count digits and emits every decoded character once.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(m) output storage. The builders store the produced output, whose decoded length may greatly exceed encoded length.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Use an unsigned rolling polynomial hash for the pattern and each equal-length text window. A matching hash triggers a full character comparison, so hash collisions cannot produce a false match. Return the first verified window.
checks.correctness: The rolling hash invariant is the polynomial hash of the current text window, using unsigned wraparound arithmetic consistently for pattern and text. Removing the outgoing weighted character, multiplying by the radix and adding the incoming character preserves that invariant. Equal hashes trigger an exact span comparison, so collisions cannot create false matches. Windows are considered from left to right, making the first verified match the required answer.
checks.workedTrace: Search text cedar-ridge for pattern ridge. The pattern has length 5. The initial window is cedar; rolling updates examine windows starting at 1 through 5 without a verified match. The window beginning at index 6 is ridge. Its hash agrees and the character comparison succeeds, so return 6.
checks.edgeCases: An empty pattern matches at index 0. A pattern longer than the text cannot match. Repeated matches return the first index; equal hashes alone never establish equality.
checks.timeDerivation: O(n + m) time when hash matches are rare; O(nm) worst-case time with repeated hash collisions, for text length n and pattern length m. KMP fallback decreases a prefix length previously increased by scans; rolling hashes cost constant time per window plus exact verification when hashes agree.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(1) auxiliary space. Prefix tables, converted strings and Java verification substrings are accounted for separately from scalar hash state.
